title: Growing Vegetables
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Raise a nursery of kale or cabbage with the class, transplant in the evening after watering the nursery, and keep a care record.

skills.key_step: The child names the practices in growing vegetables in order (site and seedbed, nursery, transplanting, watering, weeding, manure, pest control, harvesting) and says how one depends on another.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how to prepare a seedbed.
floor.question: Why break the soil fine?

steps: Choose the site; prepare the bed.

board.do: Write the cards: transplant, nursery, harvest.

listen_for: Transplant, make a nursery, sow, harvest
misconceptions.repair: Ask what you transplant if you have not sown.

misconceptions.ask: What else must be done after transplanting kale?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a weeded and an unweeded bed after three weeks.

misconceptions.ask: How are sukuma wiki leaves harvested?
misconceptions.repair: Show a kale plant picked for weeks: the stem has scars of old leaves.

misconceptions.ask: Should manure be added when preparing a vegetable bed?
misconceptions.repair: Grow kale in poor soil and in manured soil side by side.

checks.question: Name a practice after transplanting.
checks.answer: watering, weeding, manuring or pest control

skills.key_step: The child says how a nursery bed is made (good site near water, dug fine, manured, raised a little, drills, thin shallow sowing, mulch, shade, gentle watering) and why (tender seedlings are easy to care for in one small place).

floor.prerequisite: Knows how to sow tiny seeds.
floor.question: How deep are tiny seeds sown?

representations: a picture of a shade made of sticks and grass
contexts: a home nursery in a basin

board.do: Draw a nursery bed with a shade over it.
Wait for "to protect from strong sun".

listen_for: Big lumps are better for tiny seeds
misconceptions.ask: Why is the nursery soil broken to a fine crumb?
misconceptions.repair: Hide a tiny seed under a lump and under a crumb and ask which one can push through.

misconceptions.ask: How deep should you cover tiny kale seeds?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how a tiny shoot can push through a thick layer of soil.

misconceptions.ask: How should the nursery bed be watered?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to tiny seeds in a puddle.

misconceptions.ask: Why is a nursery bed given shade?
misconceptions.repair: Put one tray of seedlings in the sun and one under a shade for a hot day.

checks.question: Why are vegetables raised in a nursery first?
checks.answer: tender seedlings are easier to care for in one place

checks.question: Why is the nursery near water?

skills.key_step: The child says how to transplant (water the nursery first, lift with soil on the roots, plant in the evening at the same depth, firm, water) and care afterwards (water, shade if hot, gap, weed, protect from pests).

floor.prerequisite: Knows how a nursery is made.
floor.question: What is put over a nursery for shade?
floor.answer: a frame of sticks and dry grass

steps: Water the nursery the day before.
Lift with soil round the roots.
Plant in the evening at the same depth; firm and water.
Water, gap and weed in the weeks after.

board.do: Draw a seedling lifted with a ball of soil and one with bare roots.

misconceptions.ask: When is it best to transplant seedlings?
misconceptions.repair: Place one wilted and one shaded seedling in the sun and compare.

listen_for: Leave the bed dry so the soil falls off
misconceptions.ask: What should you do before lifting seedlings from the nursery?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which seedlings keep their roots: one pulled dry or one lifted wet with soil.

misconceptions.ask: What is done after transplanting seedlings?
misconceptions.repair: Look at two transplanted beds, one cared for and one left.

listen_for: As soon as they come up
misconceptions.ask: When are seedlings ready to transplant?
misconceptions.repair: Show a tiny and a ready seedling; ask which has the stronger roots.

checks.question: Why transplant in the evening?
checks.answer: it is cool, so seedlings lose less water
